subject.title: fix(tlon): cap SSE payload JSON.parse at 16 MiB to prevent OOM

question: Should Tlon SSE fail closed at a hard 16 MiB pending-buffer and JSON-payload limit for existing users after real behavior proof is added?
rationale: The cap closes a concrete resource-exhaustion path, but shipped Tlon SSE behavior had no payload ceiling and the PR does not prove typical Urbit event sizes in a real setup.

options.title: Accept 16 MiB After Proof
options.body: Require redacted live or production-style SSE proof, then accept the hard cap as the security and availability boundary for Tlon SSE.

options.title: Adjust The Cap Policy
options.body: Ask for a larger, documented, or otherwise Tlon-specific limit if owners believe legitimate Urbit events can exceed 16 MiB.

options.title: Pause For Tlon Owner Confirmation
options.body: Keep the PR open until a Tlon owner confirms the compatibility tradeoff or asks for a different limit strategy.

recommendation.title: Accept 16 MiB After Proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted live or production-style SSE proof, then accept the hard cap as the security and availability boundary for Tlon SSE.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest feature-history signal for Tlon ownership and shared Urbit request refactors relevant to accepting a shipped compatibility boundary.
